utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, this is IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. For the record, the accused Nikolic is not present. I am informed, Ms. Nikolic will confirm, I suppose, that he's not feeling well and that a waiver is on its way; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, my client is ill, and I believe that during the first session, we shall receive the waiver from the detention unit so that we can proceed in his absence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as your presentation is concerned, I notice the absence of Mr. Bourgon, Mr. Sarapa, and Mr. Krgovic. Good morning to you, Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Unless there are preliminaries, which I'm not informed of you, in any case, you may continue with your cross-examination. Do you think you will finish today?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The plan is to try my best, but I think I may just need a session or so on Monday but if I do finish we'll know sooner, closer to the end of the day, I would suspect but I'm hoping to get done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Pandurevic, if you keep your answers more succinct, I think it will help Mr. Ostojic end yourself, finish with his cross-examination and also for the rest of the week today. So let's start.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can we please have P378 back, we kind of ended with that late last night, which is, I don't know, it's called sometimes a war diary but it's the log book; and if we could have the assistant of the usher to give Mr. Pandurevic the original that would be helpful with leave of Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, as you are getting this -- good morning, Mr. Pandurevic, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Receiving this book here, yesterday, we kind of covered late that there were two entries that were missing of quite significant dates, the 13th and 14th; is that correct? Of July, 1995, sorry.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, can you -- if you look at this and I know you're not a handwriting expert and we've had some come through this courtroom, do you know who was making the entries on the 12th of July and the 15th? Can you tell just by looking at it if they signed it? I think in the column on each page towards the right-hand side there might be a signature and some entries which indicate who the author was.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says Milan Maric on the 12th, and as for the 15th, I think this is the signature of Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And do you know who was supposed to maintain those records for the 13th and 14th?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday, Sreten Milosevic and Dragan Jokic were supposed to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Forgive me because it was late last night --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, could we have the B/C/S page displayed on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we do that? Could you give us the reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's a little difficult because those pages are missing, but he can reference the 12th of July, and then, I think, also the 15th if they want to look at both; but in the English version it's simply page 1 through 5 but on the B/C/S version, I think Mr. Pandurevic would be able to assist us if he could just read out perhaps the ERN number of the page on the 12th but before the 15th of July then we can maybe get that up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last three digits are 689.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'm just waiting so it comes up so everyone can catch up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, just so that I'm correct, this is a book that was kept and maintained in the ordinary course of business at the Zvornik Brigade command, correct, as opposed to the IKM?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a log book of the operations duty officer to be filled in with the duty officer for a particular day. There are no missing pages here, rather, there are no entries relating to the 12th, 13th and 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You're right about that. I misspoke because that other book had missing pages but we'll get to that in a second. This one there are just no entries for the 13th and 14th, you're right.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But my question is this was kept at the forward command post; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this was kept in the cupboard of the duty operations officer in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How far away was that from the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Also what's curious to me is the entry on the 16th. Did you find it or was that one missing as well? I think it's missing actually so ...

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's missing. Nobody filled it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know why?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Milorad Trbic was the duty operations officer and why he failed to make any entries, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Same question for the 13th and 14th. Do you know why, since you seem to recall that it was Jokic, and I forget who the other person that you mentioned that was the duty officer for the 14th, why did they fail to make any entries in this book for the 13th and 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, I can only speculate. I don't know the reasons why.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who is Petko Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. He may have been someone from the MUP judging by his last name, but I'm not sure if you can help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will. He was a guy who Colonel Dragomir Vasic wanted to appoint in Srebrenica as the police chief for Srebrenica when they were living with Miroslav Deronjic and others, but we'll get his document; how about Nenad Simic, who was he?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Nenad Simic was in the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What command did he hold or which battalion or unit?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the assistant commander for moral guidance, religious and legal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: For what period of time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly. He was definitely there in July and sometime before that. A few people held this position but I think he was the one who stayed longest.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: He stayed there in 1993 as well, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he came sometime in 1993. He was a refugee from Central Bosnia or from Mount Ozren, he may have come even earlier though.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's just quickly look at 7D454, please. This, sir, as it's coming up is a document dated the 11th of November, 1993, that purports to be signed by Captain First Class Nenad Simic assistant commander for morale, guidance and religious affairs. I think if you see the date on the top of the first page then if we could please move to the second page where the signature is.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, somebody signed this on behalf of Nenad Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So, I mean, it's really not a point of my question but you recognise it's not his signature, right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the word "for" added and this is also not his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now my point is from 1993 November through July of 1993, was he your assistant commander in the Zvornik Brigade for moral guidance, religious and legal affairs?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think he was holding that position throughout the whole period.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me understand this: When did you want or have a desire to appoint Colonel Dragomir Vasic to be in that position?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did he ever hold that position, that is, Dragomir Vasic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never at the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At any other brigade or command?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Because -- and I'm sorry I don't have the transcript, and I'm going to be brief about this, and I appreciate the Court's indulgence as well as my colleagues'. I thought yesterday you had mentioned Dragomir Vasic being demobilised and that at one point he was in what command or brigade before he was demobilised and went to the MUP; do you know?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had been with the 6th Battalion but that battalion had a different numerical designation at the time. I wanted to appoint him the assistant for that battalion not the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Now, we've talked as we've seen in the last two and a half or three years that there were quite a few people with the first name Ljubo or a derivative of that name. Now we know that just from looking at some of your testimony and the records here there was a Ljubo Bojanovic, that we spent a little bit of time talking about yesterday, and I'm sure we'll get back to him. Do you remember any other Ljubos in the Zvornik Brigade in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment, I cannot remember any other name in the command of the Zvornik Brigade apart from Ljubo Bojanovic. Maybe it's best if we looked at the list of the officers in the command so that we can be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll get through that. Who is Ljubo Bijatovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a man called Bejatovic. He was the commander of the 7th Battalion in July 1995 but I cannot remember his first name. I don't think it was Ljubo. I think his first name was Drago.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I did see a reference in one of the paperwork calling him Drago as well. How about Ljubislav Strbac, do you remember him at all?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name was Ljubisav Strbac, and we used to call him Strki.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what was his position in July of 1995 to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the assistant of the Chief of Staff for organisation, mobilisation personnel affairs for a certain period of time. I think he was attached to that organ at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about one of the people on your witness list, Ljubo Eric, what was he in July of 1995, you remember him, of course. He's one of your witnesses; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember him. He was with the 2nd Romanija. He was the commander of the combat group in Krivaja 95 operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what other position did he hold in July of 1995 other than he was commander of a combat group in Krivaja 95. After or before that operation, what was his title, if you will?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. He was with the 2nd Romanija Brigade and I don't know which positions he held as per establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What was the name of Obrenovic's driver again? Do you remember his name or at least his first name?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljubisa Danojlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And who is Ljubo Dejanovic. Do you remember him at all?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This last name doesn't sound familiar to me, probably it was mispronounced, therefore, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It happens a lot to me. It's actually in an entry I came across it, but we'll talk about it a little later. Any other Ljubos that you can think of other than these six or seven that we've mentioned thus far because -- or a derivative of either Ljubisa or Ljubislav or Ljubomir or any of those types that you could ...

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljubo Beara, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Any others that you can remember?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljubo Sobot.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And we talked about him. He is the food with the intercept that earlier the Prosecution alleged that it was Ljubisa Beara that was on that intercept and then later other evidence showed that it was actually Ljubo Sobot, we believe, and dealing with Mladic and some food and what not. So we talked about him in the trial. Anyone else that you can come up with?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljubisa Simic, the president of the Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's a good point. He came here. Is he related in any way to Nenad Simic, the guy who was your commander or assistant commander for legal, religious and moral affairs?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I was not interested in those relations.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. Now, in sticking with P378, I believe, that you have in front of you, I'd like to go over a couple entries that are actually made in the book. We know we can't go over the 13th, 14th and 16th, but before I go on to those entries, can you tell me why, after the 15th or I'm sorry the 17th of July -- strike that. Why, sir, after the 18th of July, does the entire month get skipped as well as August and then entries start to appear in September? Do you have any reason or do you know why that would happen?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see August here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In my version we go from July 18th and you can help us with that and all of a sudden the next entry is the 16th of the 9th month and then below that the 17th of the 9th month and so on so ...

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 18th of July, the 19th of July, 21st, 23rd, 24th of July and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you look on the English version, it may be just a mistake it just shows the 9th of the 16th and 17th, but thank you for that. Let's turn to the 11th of July, 1995. The 11th of July, 1995, please, on Exhibit P378 if you could open it and take a look at it. We do have that actual entry, so I'd like to ask you a couple questions about that.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought you were going to ask me something about the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I am, actually, but I wanted to give you the benefit of the book. Now, focussing your attention on this page, and I think we're going to try it get it up on B/C/S, and, Mr. Pandurevic, if you could also just help me out by giving us the last three numbers --

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 688, the last three digits are 688.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the entry of the 11th of July, 1995, who made those entries, to the best of your understanding, looking at the signature block, I guess.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the entries on the 11th were made by Ljubo Bojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could scroll down to the bottom of the page in the English version, the entry of 2030 hours, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you read it for us, please, the entry in that short block of four lines?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can: "Chief ordered wake up call for all units at 0400 hours and the commanders are to report at 0400 hours and brief about the situation in the battalions."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who is the chief that Ljubo Bojanovic is referring to there?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljubo Bojanovic was probably referring to Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: He wasn't referring to you; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Because you weren't there; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm just pointing it out because sometimes Ljubo Bojanovic can make a mistake, and he would say instead of Chief of Staff he would put the commander; and this might be a little misleading at least because it may be indicative that you came back to Zvornik on the 11th of July and then you asked for a wake up call, and you wanted these commanders to report to a briefing in the battalions. I mean, without your testimony we wouldn't know that this is really -- that it was Dragan Obrenovic that he really means even though he's passed away, and we don't have his testimony on that point; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's probably wrong translation. My name is not mentioned anywhere here. Chief means Dragan Obrenovic and later on, when they say commander, that refers to battalion commanders to be woken up and report about the situation in the battalions. It was not any mistake on Ljubo's part, I am not mentioned anywhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You were the chief of the Zvornik Brigade, were you not?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was the commander. Nobody called me chief. I didn't like that word at all. It's not a military term.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we look at the entry on the 12th of July made by a different person, I think Milan Maric at 1310 hours, he's more explicit, and he says at 1300 hours, the Chief of Staff had ordered certain things; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Ljubo Bojanovic could have written it on the 11th of July, Chief of Staff, could he not?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but he used the word "chief" more often.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now just help me with this as we're scrolling down through this document. It's here at the 12th of July, the entry at 1630 hours; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, this talks about a military police platoon with the Commander Jasikovac went to carry out the task; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who ordered this?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I see that the Chief of Staff had ordered, so it came from above. So this probably refers to this platoon as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. A couple more questions, if you don't mind, to clarify on this document. And then if we can please look at the next page which is the 15th of July, 1995. Because again as you remember the 13th and 14th were not recorded. Okay. Now, here there is an entry that I'd like to discuss with you at 1350 hours and I direct your attention to that.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Basically I'm going to read it in English but you can read it for us if you like. It says: "Some elements of unit returned from Zepa, and they joined the action of blocking and destroying the group of Turks." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, does it say anywhere there about your order or your mission or your goal that Krstic gave you that we talked about yesterday at 1041 or 10.00 on the 15th of July to capture anybody? Does it reference that at all in this entry?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've simplified Krstic's order.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, let me just stop you for a second. I didn't simplify it. You completely ignored it when you gave your direct evidence, so I'm just now going to talk to you about specifically the things he shared with you, so forgive me for telling you but I'm not simplified it. It's in the order, you got it both orally and you got it in writing, so share with me that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, stop arguing the way you are and with the tone you are with the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you answer, Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, Mr. Ostojic, I'm trying to provide brief answers instructed by the Chamber, but your questions are three times longer than my answers. I don't dispute what Krstic ordered. I was quite clear about that, but you're just focussing on some sort of arrest and detention. I didn't arrest anyone, and I didn't take anyone in and you can't arrest a division.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't even know what that means to be very honest with you, Mr. Pandurevic, but I'm sure that your lawyer will clarify it on re-direct or at any time. I'm asking you this: Did Krstic give you an oral --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't be sure of that. If you're not clear about it you can ask questions yourself. You have no guarantee that Mr. Haynes will clear it up for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. President, I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, did Krstic give you an order to block, destroy, and/or capture the Muslims that were coming from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He assigned me a task, and I was to block the penetration of the 28th Division and the joining up of that division with the forces of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that was the extent of his order to you and your assignment; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: He didn't mention anything about capturing anybody?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the course of the battle perhaps someone would have been captured, that's what happened subsequently from the 28th onwards.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: From the 18th, interpreter's correction. From the 18th onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, maybe it was a poor translation or an unartful question on my part. I'm not asking you what could have happened, I'm asking you did Krstic verbally, orally and/or in writing tell you that you should capture the Bosnian Muslims that are escaping from Srebrenica and going through Zvornik? And this is a good chance where you could just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order had to do with that too, that they weren't prisoners who had previously been brought to Zvornik, you want to link this up but that's not what it's about. These people had already been arrested and you know who did that, just as I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Those people who were arrested and detained, do you know that the civilian authorities were the ones who brought them from Bratunac to Zvornik, and it was your military police, sir, from Zvornik Brigade who brought them from Bratunac to Zvornik. Do you know that? Or are you denying that as well?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not denying that I heard about those matters, and I have testified about them; but I don't know who brought those people to Bratunac and then who organised a column and an escort and who took those people to Zvornik, nor do I know why they chose to take them to Zvornik; but I'm sure that there are people here who can be quite explicit about what happened and provide you can clear statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever talk to one of your buddies, Colonel Dragomir Vasic, as to what he thought his role was because I know you spent an awful lot of time talking about parallel events, and let's look at where Mr. Pandurevic was and then let's look at a log book that may support it. What about the MUP documents? Did you look parallel to that or even ask Dragomir Vasic what he knew about the prisoners in 1995? Did you do that at all?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vasic and I are not friends, not in the way that you think. I didn't have any MUP documents, and I didn't examine them. I didn't speak to Vasic about his activities during that period of time. I heard about all this parallel events as we've been calling them on the basis of a report on Dragan Obrenovic and on the basis of documents from the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right. But wait a second, you did talk to him during that period because you even told us that you met with him on the 15th of July when you came from the Srebrenica general area, if I can call it that, back to the -- to the command post in Zvornik, he was actually in Obrenovic's office and you ran into him there. So you did see him at least on the 15th; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw him. I knew that tasks were to control the territory and to provide security for Serbian villages. I assumed that that's what they did and he did, in fact, do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How do you know if you never talked to him that he did, in fact, do that? Did you talk to him or didn't you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well that was his task, his regular task. He must have done it and I could see from the documents from his reports it's stated where his units were engaged, where they had been deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know what his assignment was on July 13th through 15th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know on the basis of the documents that we can see now here or, rather, the documents that I saw in the course of these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What was it? What was his assignment?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, you've referred to his documents most frequently had to do with providing security for roads, for direct access routes to the town of Zvornik and had to do with establishing or setting up checkpoints and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about one of the documents on the 15th where he says killing 8.000 Bosnian Muslims; do you remember that at all or did that kind of slip?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it was on the 15th. I think that document was dated the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you really look at my question, that's why I said from the 13th to the 15th, do you know what his assignment was? Who gave him the assignment to kill Bosnian Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether anyone gave him such an assignment, nor do I know whether he killed those Muslims; but I remember an intercept where one co-accused said these people from the MUP don't want to do anything. I don't know what he had in mind. And Vasic in those reports emphasised the role that the MUP played, and he emphasised his own role as if he was the only player in the field and no one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now when you say player in the field, I just want to make sure I don't step all over your unique distinction between zone of defence and zone of responsibility. What field are you talking about, sir? Is it in the field of the zone of defence that you've shared with us or is it the broader area of the zone of responsibility that the Prosecution claims that the Zvornik Brigade had, which field?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The zone of defence of the Zvornik Brigade was the one we saw on the map and it's where the soldiers of the Zvornik Brigade were deployed. All other territory outside that area which is inhabited by people who are involved in their daily activities, well for the control and order of that territory, there was just the MUP, that was their responsibility if enemy forces appeared in the area, if there were infiltrated and if they engaged in combat then the brigade would be activated to prevent such events from occurring.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did Miroslav Deronjic ever come to the Zvornik Brigade in July of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Thank you. 1995.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well we'll go into an entry which has his name in one of your duty officers' books on the 17th or 18th of July in a few minutes here. Do you know that in July of 1995, President Karadzic appointed him to be some commissioner for Srebrenica? Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first part that you mentioned I remember. In the log book for the 17th, it said that Miroslav Deronjic wanted me to release some communications officers to the command or the Chief of Staff for something to do with the PTT or communications. I can't remember receiving that note. I don't remember, or I didn't know what position he held at the time that he had been appointed to be civilian commissioner by the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And we all know, but just to make sure that you know, you know that Miroslav Deronjic came from Bratunac; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he lived in Bratunac. He was probably born somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You told us about a meeting that you had with Krstic, and I think you even said Mladic in Bratunac in July of 1995. Was Deronjic at that meeting as well?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th, at that meeting of the command of the Bratunac Brigade, well at that meeting, only soldiers were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And just to the best of your recollection, I know it's been a few years, but do you know approximately what time that meeting was on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's a well-known historical fact now, it was around 2200 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's look at Exhibit 1D690, please. If we can also have the B/C/S version or -- looks like we don't have a B/C/S version but we can all read on paragraph number 4, and I'll read it out loud so you can get the full thing. This looks like it's a decision from Dr. Radovan Karadzic dated the 11th of July, 1995, and really I wanted to ask you about -- I mean we can talk about any portion of it, but I want to highlight paragraph 4, if you don't mind because it says, paragraph 4 here: "The commissioner shall ensure that all civilian and military organs treat all citizens who participated in combat against the Army of Republika Srpska as prisoners of war, and ensure that the civilian population can freely choose where they will live or move to." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there any discussion in that meeting on the 11th of July, 1995, about Miroslav Deronjic and him being in charge of the prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no. I don't know when this decision from the president arrived, at what time of day, and I can't see that he was directly responsible for the prisoners here. The military authorities and the civilian authorities had to take joint care of the prisoners and other civilians who wanted to stay or leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll take a look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, Mr. Ostojic. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can those who don't speak English see the whole of the document on the screen, please. It's not really fair to any of them, including the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I fully agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... there must be B/C/S, it is originally in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's around, we can get it relatively easily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's see if we can get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I can move away from this and come back to this exhibit for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the intercept between Karadzic and Deronjic which is P1149, and I think it's A and then the B/C/S version is P1149B.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Pandurevic, you may recall this exhibit since you were here during the trial. It purports to be a intercept between Deronjic and an intermediary who's talking to Karadzic, and apparently Karadzic is transferring some information between this intermediary and Deronjic; and it's at 2010 hours, 2010, and when it comes up I'll give you a chance to look at it.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so that the record is clear, Mr. Pandurevic, and to be fair to you, you remember this because you saw it during the trial while you were here; right? You don't have an independent information about this conversation; I'm correct about that, right? Or do you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite understandable. How could I have been aware of it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sometimes the record is awkward, and it says some things we don't necessarily mean. Now here in this conversation that we discussed at this court briefly, it's a conversation between, as I mentioned, Deronjic and Karadzic and his intermediary; and as you can recall and as you can read here it's Deronjic and Karadzic who are talking about approximately thousands but 2.000 Bosnian Muslims who are moving through an area and then they are discussing where they should be maintained or held. In the last couple entries where they have X and D for Deronjic and X presumably for the intermediary, it says not to put them in the warehouses but to put them somewhere else. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can read out this passage as to what conclusions one draws on the basis of the passage, well, that's a matter for each individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you know where these prisoners, the 2.000 or so, I guess in the middle of it says about two for the time being after he was asked how many thousands, so let's just go with the 2.000 for now. Do you know where these prisoners are at this time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know, I didn't even know that they existed at the time of this conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know why Karadzic wants the prisoners or Deronjic wants the prisoners moved from wherever they were?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, we know, at least historically, from some facts in this case that in Bratunac, there were some that were detained and as you yourself say, although I know your position clearly, it's not your position because it's outside the zone of defence, that there were some prisoners transferred over to Zvornik, are these the guys? Because look at the time frame, it's the 13th; and I know you're not involved in this, sir, but I just wanted to see if you could maybe help us understand this because you asked me earlier today, Well we know who transferred the prisoners and how they were transferred. I'm trying to help that issue out -- I know I'm going fast. I'm sorry. So here we have the 13th at 2010 hours, a conversation that was captured between Deronjic and Karadzic through his intermediary and they are talking about 2.000 prisoners, and they are saying we got to put them somewhere and we've got to move them to some warehouse or put them somewhere else, could this possibly you think even remotely be the 2.000 that were ultimately transferred to Zvornik in the next day or so or that evening?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has already told you at the time he didn't even know about their existence, how can you expect him to tell you that ultimately these were the 2.000 that were sent to the Zvornik area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: He can just tell me if he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you shouldn't ask the question. I don't think it's for him to tell you, to face you with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me try it another way. Thank you. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know where these 2.000 men ultimately ended up that Deronjic and Karadzic and his intermediary are talking about, even after the fact, did you ever find out what happened to these men?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything specific about these 2.000 whether they are included in the number of people who were brought to the territory of Zvornik. But I can clarify something else, Deronjic received that information about the presence of 2.000 prisoners, but I don't know from whom so there was someone else. In addition to Deronjic, who was aware of this because Deronjic didn't go into the field to see how many people had been arrested, I don't know why he is addressing the president, why he didn't address Mladic at the same time with regard to the same issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever talk to Mr. Deronjic before you were indicted in this case about the events that unfolded in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever talk to Mr. Deronjic when he was detained here at the UNDU before he passed away?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I saw him on two occasions when we played sports together, but I never discussed the events in Srebrenica with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you this, because I want to change gears although talking about these civilians. There was a lot spent about this MNI issue which is the minimum number of individuals, and I know you heard a lot of testimony about it through various experts, et cetera. Now, when you said and when your Zvornik Brigade whether it was under your command or not when they were conducting these ambushes, did they attain any level of success? Do you know if they actually killed or as you say destroyed the enemy at any time in those early days of July 13th, 14th, 15th, 16th, 17th, even?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To a certain extent but I don't know how successful they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know in some of your combat -- interim combat reports and combat reports it does discuss that there were huge losses or enormous losses and all that, and I'm not going to go into that right now. I want to know generally speaking when those people are shot and killed, and even Butler agreed those were legitimate military combat engagements so he had no problem if you are in a fight like that, in the unfortunate event of war, but where were those people ultimately buried; do you know?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you that there were quite a lot of people who were killed when breaking through from Srebrenica to Tuzla, many of them remained in the forests, and that's where they were killed, as far as I have understood. Some of the bodies that remain there were gathered and collected and buried, but I don't have precise information about this. Perhaps some of those bodies are still there in those forests.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But who would, if you don't, sir, as the command of the Zvornik Brigade, who at that time would have had that best information for us so he could help me with that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult for me to help you. If someone was killed in Ravne Polje, Kamenica Crska, Udrc, Velja Glava, Snagovo in Baljkovica, we would then search the field and all the bodies found in the territory of Baljkovica were buried in the territory of Motovska Koso.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm aware you still have P378. If we could just go back to that entry of July 11th, 1995, and I just want to tie up a loose end, if I can. This is an entry that and again you corrected me, and thank you for that, that I thought when I read it initially years or months ago that at 2030 hours when it said chief ordered wake up call, I thought they were referring to you, and that you were present at the Zvornik Brigade, and you told us you weren't and I accept that. Help me reconcile this because we also want to look at Exhibit P322 which is a regular combat report dated July 12, 1995, and you covered it a little bit on your direct. And it seems to be with a block signature with your name on it, but you weren't there. So just when we get that up, and I want to make sure that you look at it so I'm right. I'm sorry, if you could wait there so we could make sure that Mr. Pandurevic has the date. Sir, are you following me? We're looking at Exhibit P378, the late July 11th entry which says: "Chief ordered a wake-up call at 4.00 and that the commanders are to report in order to get a brief of the situation." And then we are looking at the next day of the regular combat report dated July 12th, 1995 and you are welcome to look at the whole report, but just if we can look at the second page which I believe has your block or third page -- forgive me, no, I was right the first time, the second page. Yes they put it up on B/C/S, I'm waiting for the English, sorry about that. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And just reconcile it because if I look at these two documents because I was in error before, and I just want to make sure the court doesn't see it incorrectly either. Although it says chief in this P378 that I was an order for commanders to come there and despite the fact that we have this other document that has your printed block on it, it has nothing to do with you, you weren't there at all; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there, and there was the duty officers who inscribed the name of the chief, someone inscribed my name and this shows that one didn't know the rules. Those who weren't professionals -- well because someone wasn't professional someone might be held criminally responsible. Now I should have said deputy commander here. And Dragan Obrenovic, in the 14th in his report, it says the Chief of Staff, the Major, Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I did look at the 14th and I also looked at the 13th. That report has again your name on it even though you weren't there on the 12th or the 13th of July; correct? And we can go if you'd like really quickly we don't even have to go that quickly, 325, P325, please. Mr. Pandurevic, I don't take issue with you not being there and I just know that sometimes what's written is a mistake, and that's why we'd just like to clarify it; and I think there is quite a few mistakes but we'll talk about that probably later. So let's look at P325. Here also is yet another example -- I'm sorry, and then if we could have the next page with the signature block and this is a daily combat report.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same thing. We had some reports where the name of the operations officer, operations duty officer and the commander were signed, but when they were there and when they weren't; so these people were acting automatically. It was through inertia that it was done in this way, and they didn't understand military rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now since we have P325 there, who was -- who wrote this report or who sent it out with your name block on it? Which was the individual?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is the 13th of July, SM, that could be Sreten Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about the one before that on P322, which is the July 12th regular combat report?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: They'll bring it up. It just takes a little time sometimes. P322, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I see page 2 in the Serbian, please. I think that this MM stands for Milan Maric, but it's not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. But are those Sreten Milosevic and Milan Maric, although it's not clear, were they reliable type of soldiers in your Zvornik Brigade at that time in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were as they were. Those were reserve officers, Sreten Milosevic was assistant for logistics, he was an economist. He was familiar, quite familiar with the job whereas on the other hand, he wasn't so familiar with military rules and regulations. Maric finished the faculty for All People's Defence, so, therefore, he was not involved in the procedures and things that we professional military personnel were skilled and trained for.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now let me go to the July 16th, 1995 day and the issues that you talked a little bit about. On July 16th, 1995, did Ljubo Bojanovic ever tell you anything about vehicles from Banja Luka coming and going to the school in Orahovac? Did he tell you anything about that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember any specific contact with him at the moment, but I think there is a note in the work log that Ljubo reported that a truck came from the 16th Krajina Company and that he was to send it to Orahovac, if that's what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That is what I'm referring to. How about Obrenovic, did he on the 16th of July, 1995, tell you or ask you about the men who came from Bratunac who were in Orahovac and asking you for instructions as to what to do with those men? Did you ever have that discussion with Obrenovic on July 16th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I sent Obrenovic to meet this company from the 16th Krajina Corps to give them the task. It might happen that in the meantime, soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade turn up as well and Obrenovic asked me what to do with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well let's take a look at Exhibit 377, which again, is one of those duty officer notebooks or log books; and if we can, with the Court's permission, the usher's assistance have the Prosecutor give Mr. Pandurevic the original and again it's 377. Sir, I'm going to direct your attention ERN 0293-5771, so the last four numbers are 5771.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And let me just help here and get caught up myself. We have, if the Court remembers, the English translation which was, I think, made with certain markings on the side, yes, I know you have it, I just want to make sure, which were actually later added to identify who individuals were. I'm looking at the entry with the ERN on the bottom 5769, and in the middle of that entry, it says: "Men from Bratunac are in Orahovac. Obrenovic asked the commander what to do with them at 1920 hours." Did you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, did Obrenovic ask you -- I mean he's talking about the commander, would that be you on the 16th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And so although little slightly different I'm not going to question what -- from what you told us just moments ago regarding this issue, it was Obrenovic who asked you and told you about these men from Bratunac, did he not?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What was he asking? What do you mean by or what did he mean by "what to do with them"?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember details but probably he referred whether they should be joined with the men from Krajina or should they be sent to another axis, I'm not sure. I think that later on they joined the battalion in the area of Crni Vrh.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At the time at 1920 hours on July 16th, 1995, did you ask Obrenovic what the men from Bratunac were doing in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask Obrenovic about what they were doing there. I think there is also a note about the time when they arrived. What I knew was that the soldiers from Krajina were arriving, and Obrenovic was sent there to receive them. So at that time, he must have also come across the soldiers from the Bratunac Brigade; and, therefore, he asked me what to do with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So he didn't tell you anything that these men were Bratunac were in Orahovac because they were involved in any executions or detention of POWs, did he?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These men didn't take part in the executions. These men came to assist, and they were deployed on the road at Crni Vrh.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the next page or two in English, it's actually on the lower portion same date, 16th July, last four numbers 5771 with ERN, and it starts, sir, with 2210 hours, the entry there, the fifth line down. After there is a brief discussion with Pilica, do you see Pilica, at 0800 hours. Maybe I can ...

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now that entry, the first one here: "At 2210 hours," it goes on to say they are talking about a loader and excavator and a dump truck, and it should be going to Pilica at 8.00; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, this says that it was conveyed to Jokic and Milosevic; and I think those are Dragan Jokic and Sreten Milosevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now these are two individuals that you had talked to on the 16th of July -- well --

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I almost said 15th, and we wouldn't want to mess up the record. You didn't talk to him on the 15th, but you talked to him on the 16th of July, 1995. Did they share with you that they were sending these excavators and loaders and dump trucks to Pilica when you talked to him on the 16th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where did you acquire this information that I talked to them on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I thought you said yes and then that's why I -- did you ever talk to him on the 16th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to them on the 15th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to them. We saw the intercept, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about on the 17th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to Jokic on the 18th relating the engagement of engineering machinery, and he said that Trbic had told him that a machine should be sent to Pilica or rather Branjevo, as it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever talk to Sreten Milosevic about that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The information I received from Jokic was sufficient for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of July 1995, you had no knowledge of this activity by -- which was conveyed to you by Jokic and Milosevic; is that what you're saying? You only found that out on the 18th; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that from Jokic, that is about the machinery being engaged, but he told me earlier that the machines were already engaged on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But it looks from this note that they were engaged on what date, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here in the morning at 8.00 in Pilica, so if this entry is at 2210, that would mean the next day, and I can only speculate why this request was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know, maybe we misunderstood each other, but the entry in this request was actual made on the 16th, and these excavators and loaders were sent on the next day being the 17th of July; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now let's go to the next entry there, which is the one I really wanted to talk to you about, and that's Ljubo Bojanovic's entry. Did you talk to Ljubo Bojanovic at all on the 16th of July, 1995, when you were either at the IKM or at the -- wherever your observation post or wherever you were on the 16th? Did you talk to him at all?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember all these communications with everyone; however, this note indicates that from either the IKM or the Orahovac, Ljubo is telling the duty operations officer where to send the company station which shows -- only goes to show that Ljubo was in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not really that interested in Ljubo being in the field, but it's really the vehicle from the Banja Luka company station, that's what he's talking about; right? And Ljubo is reporting that the vehicles should go where? Where should this vehicle go?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This company had arrived earlier, and it was in the area of Orahovac. It was received by Dragan Obrenovic. Ljubo Bojanovic was probably involved in that too. A company station is a vehicle that was late, they didn't know its whereabouts, so it was said as soon as it arrived in Zvornik it should be sent to Orahovac and be linked up there with the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But in the English translation, it actually says that the school in Orahovac, it does not say that in B/C/S, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it says the school in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure because you didn't mention it. Now, was that part of the Zvornik Brigade's zone of defence or zone of responsibility that one of your guys, Ljubo Bojanovic is sending a vehicle from the Banja Luka company station to Orahovac, but particularly in Orahovac to this one school in Orahovac on the 16th of July, 1995? Whose zone is that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A vehicle cannot enter school buildings, but units can be deployed in the territory while waiting to be engaged in combat. They can march along the road. If this company was travelling from Bijeljina to Zvornik, it just passed through that, and it stayed for a while and in Orahovac and later on went on to search the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not talking about physically going into the school but the vehicle was going, I guess, so it's easier for you to understand, near the school or at the school or around the school in Orahovac; but in any event, what I'm curious to know is did Ljubo Bojanovic since you had some conversations with him at this critical time period when you returned to the forward command post, did he discuss this with you? Because at one point I recall you saying that Ljubo said he saw some buses and -- with people in it, but they just kind of passed. He didn't know they were going to Orahovac or anywhere else for that matter much less in the school or near the school. Did he share this with you on July 16th, 1995, at approximately, and we're guessing here between 2200 hours and 2330 hours, I'm just looking at the two dates. I don't really know what time it was but ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are mixes up the dates in two different situations. Ljubo mentioned to me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Ostojic and Mr. Pandurevic equally, you are creating a few problems for the interpreters, particularly the French booth, so please slow down both of you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sorry about that. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic -- sorry, and I will give you a chance to answer. I know you were in the middle of it, but just so that we are clear on the record, you were going to explain to me that I'm mixing up the dates. When did you talk to Ljubo Bojanovic when you returned back from the Srebrenica area from the Zvornik Brigade command and/or IKM, when?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to him on the afternoon of the 15th when he came to the IKM after a conversation with Brano Grujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And did you talk to him, sir, ever again after that, meaning -- sorry -- strike that. Let me ask you this, did you talk to him on the 16th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't discuss this topic with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking if you discussed this topic. Did you talk to Ljubo Bojanovic at all on the 16th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, these are somewhat impossible requests put to me to recall each and every single communication with each and every individual. I may have probably issued some task to Ljubo Bojanovic. I know that on the 16th and 17th he was searching the ground. I probably gave him a task on the evening of the 16th, or it could have been Dragan Obrenovic who did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, if you don't remember, just tell us you don't have a recollection of that. How about on the 17th, do you remember discussing with Ljubo Bojanovic this topic or let's just even broaden it, the topic of POWs on the 17th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I ever discussed this subject with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me understand why not. If he told you that he saw the buses of POWs going through, and then later you have information that these people were executed, why didn't you come up to him and say, Ljubo, as your commander, what happened? You told me they went through Zvornik. Did you ever have that discussion with him?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljubo told me what he purportedly knew, and that was not nearly enough to provide any detail; and, therefore, I didn't ask him anything else about this subject because in the meantime, I had received information from Dragan Obrenovic. I also --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't understand the last part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Ostojic. Mr. Pandurevic, the interpreters didn't catch the last part of your answer. If you look at the screen, it stops after, "I had received information from Dragan Obrenovic." Then you said something else, if you could repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Since Mr. Ostojic is insisting on the name Ljubo, I just added that I didn't talk to any Ljubo at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Shall we have the break, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you -- yeah, whatever you'd like, Mr. President, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are very gentle. Let's have a 25-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just before we begin, a couple of housekeeping matters. On page 19, line 16, it was brought to my attention to the date was placed, and we were discussing I think the decision by Karadzic, it was mentioned as it being the 19th, but it should be the 11th, I think, that's what it says. And then also when we were discussing with Mr. Pandurevic Exhibit 1D690, we didn't have the B/C/S translation, that exhibit is also in evidence as P10, so if we can just bring that up now as well with the B/C/S just to give him an opportunity to take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, let's start with that. The correction of the date will be looked into, looked after, in due course. Did we get the numbers, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So it's P10 that we are looking at, Mr. Pandurevic, and I apologise for not having that in B/C/S for you earlier. I think I was focussing on paragraph number 4, can you read that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can: " The commissioner shall ensure that the civilian and military organs treat all citizens who participated in combat against the Army of Republika Srpska as prisoners of war, and ensure that the civilian population can freely choose where they will live or move to."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know - thank you - during the direct, you asked questions about the word "bezbednost" or "obezbeditie" as we see it in paragraph 4, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context or in this sentence, grammatically one can say that they will undertake measures and do so and so as it goes on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, we don't need that exhibit for now. I think I mentioned it, but it's dated the 11th of July, 1995, as you see on the bottom; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Because I think I misspoke earlier, so I wanted to make sure that it's clear. Now let's take a look at a couple of exhibits or intercepts, actually and if we could have P1102 on the screen for you, sir. And just so the record is clear, I think it's either A in English or there is a different version with the letter D, Delta, in English, same number, P1102. I don't necessarily -- I don't know that it matters which one but just so the Court's aware of it, there's two exhibits. And, Mr. Pandurevic, for you we would use P1102B which is the B/C/S version and I just want to be careful that there is no name on it, so I would probably ask that it not be broadcast but I think it can be -- or it could not be so we should not broadcast it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm told it is under seal, so no broadcast and also use your discretion on what to mention and what not to mention in public session, otherwise we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is an intercept that was apparently captured on the 12th of July, 1995 at 7.40 in the morning. It involves Obrenovic; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that one of the speakers allegedly is Obrenovic, but as I see it, it was not Obrenovic who took part in this conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And help us with that because it does say Obrenovic, you're correct. Who took part in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, the caller, the one who called Obrenovic's number, the telephone rings, and he is expecting Obrenovic to answer it. Someone else picked up and says "hello." The caller says, "Obrenovic who?" Not Obrenovic, this is a form of addressing the person by the name whereas there is no response because obviously the one who answered was not Obrenovic, but he didn't state his name, therefore, no record of it; and then the question is: "Where is your commander?" And the conversation then proceeds as we see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the response to "Where is your commander?" Who are they referring to? He asked for Obrenovic, then he asked for the commander was he asking for you then? And it's the 12th of July. I know you weren't there but the answer is, "As far as I know, he's here."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, Mr. Ostojic. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm going to make an inquiry as to the relevance of this. Throughout the course of the morning, Mr. Ostojic has prefaced questions about the reports of the 12th and 13th of July and entries in the duty officers' notebook by saying, Of course I accept you were not there. Does he or doesn't he? When I says I accept you were not there. Is that a genuine expression or are these wholly disingenuous questions because if he doesn't accept that he shouldn't preface all his questions in that way, and it seems to me this is a line of examination that goes quite contrary to all the acceptances that he's placed on the record this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to comment on that, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is very genuine, and if he says he wasn't there; but I think the record shows perhaps other things, and it will help us because there are instances in the record that certain people mention our client; and yet if his position is that people -- and there are entries indicating his presence different from his testimony, it should apply to all of us, but it is genuine. I'm not being disingenuous at all with the witness. If he tells us he wasn't there at the 12th, that's his position. But if it bothers him that I preface it with that, I won't preface it with that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes, do you wish to comment further?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, if he accepts he wasn't there this morning, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again reading, Mr. Ostojic, from what he said and what we have in the transcript, I'm not sure that he does accept it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If he says it, I'm accept it, but it's not my burden of proof. It's really a question that should be directed towards the Prosecution whether they accept it or not. I accept what Mr. Pandurevic says, if he says he wasn't there. But I don't know why it's directed at me but if I can proceed and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well then let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now here, sir, just so we get it clear because there is some entries with these intercepts that we were confused, and there's certain things that the Prosecution says they mean and -- so here it says: "As far as I know, he's here." This person asked for the commander. Were they talking about Obrenovic at that time, July 12th, 1995, or were they talking about you and the response saying: "The commander is here." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other participant in the conversation, I don't know his identity, he may have been referring to Obrenovic when he asked where is the commander. It might have been someone from the corps command, Zivanovic. The corps commander knew exactly where I was, and he wouldn't be looking for me in Zvornik on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm glad you clarified that. Now let's look at another exhibit, P1103. Just so we have the date this is also July 12th, 1995, at 0755 hours. Let me know, Mr. Pandurevic, when you've had an opportunity to look at the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is also under seal, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Please don't broadcast it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there a printed version of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think there is, but I don't have it in my version.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All I want to do is focus your attention, it says here: "General, I spoke with Mane. Do you know who the reference to Mane is?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably Mane Djuric, Vasic's deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear with respect to this exhibit, P1103 it's the 12th of July, 1995, and as I said 0755 hours. The next line right after that it says he left his hotel, et cetera, one of his companies is up there with our bulldozer man there in Konjevic Polje; do you see that entry?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about Vasic's man, Mane Djuric, and what he was doing with a bulldozer man on the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, I really have to clarify this. You have interpreted this as if it's the first time you've seen this conversation. Mane didn't do anything with bulldozers. This participant told the general that there's a company of Manes in Konjevic Polje up there with that man of ours with the bulldozers. So it's the engineering battalion from the Drina Corps. No one operated bulldozers.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't want really to belabour the point, but here X is saying he left the hotel and is on his way home, who do you think he's referring to if he says, Hello, General, I've spoken to Mane. The next entry is good. Then the witness or the person who said, I spoken to Mane, he says he left the hotel and is on his way home. Do you he's talking about someone other than Mane?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know that they are talking about Mane. We're wasting time for no purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, we're not. And then he goes on to say that he'll call you from there to update you, and it says one of his companies is up there with the bulldozer man; so I just don't know really your explanation doesn't really fit with the plain reading of this. If he says one of his companies, and he's talking about him and he, was he talking about Mane the whole time or someone else?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to read out the first three paragraphs to put things into context. "Hello, General. You've spoken with Mane. X tells the general that he's spoken to Mane. Y or the general says: "Good." It continues with what he had to say about Mane, and he says the following: "He left the hotel and is on his way home. He'll call you from there to update you." So he's going to call the general to inform him about everything and the person speaking with the general then continues. "One of his companies is up there with that man of ours with the bulldozers." He's trying to refer to the 5th Engineering Battalion and he again says, "here in Konjevic Polje," so we're talk being Mane.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay that's what I thought. I misunderstood you then I apologise. Then let's go to the next exhibit, P1126, please. This is kind of an interesting exhibit. It's dated, I think, the 13th of July, and it's at -- so again P1126, and we do have the printed version of this and please, we shouldn't broadcast it because there are initials and names on the printed version in B/C/S. I think it's actually on the B/C/S the last page of this document. I don't have that actually written as A, B, C or D, but I can -- we can put it on the ELMO possibly. If you go to the next page, the entry is at 0910 hours, so 9.10 in the morning. So with the Court's permission and the usher to assist us, to put this briefly on the ELMO. It's P1126A for the English version. I think we could put that on the screen, and we do have it now on the e-court. Thank you. Sir, I'm he focussing your attention on the bottom portion of this intercept that is taken on the 13th of July at 19 -- 13th of July, 1995, at 9.10 in the morning. It's a conversation between two unknown individuals X and Y, and I'm sure you don't know who they are; but they're talking about moving something to Zvornik. Do you see that? I think it starts with: "And that's the closest" --

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- "and what should I do now?" Y says: "No, no, to Zvornik, they should send them to Zvornik." X says: "To Zvornik? " Y says: "Yes, yes, it's not possible because Milici ..." and then it doesn't have much after that in English anyway; do you see that? Then it goes on to say: "X: Well I don't have any people, I don't have them." Y says: No, not you." In English it says formal, "but the one who brings him it, and tell him to Zvornik." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. I saw the next page too.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, we've heard a lot of evidence, and the Prosecution has brought witnesses and some experts, I think even, on these intercepts, who are these people who are talking at 9.10 on the 13th of July, 1995, if you know?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: X and Y according to what we have here. Since Milici is referred to, and it says -- I assume that the reference is to wounded people. I know nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
