utterances.text: Now, do you know, sir, that our position is that Ljubisa Beara never had any intention to put or wasn't involved in any discussion to place POWs in Zvornik at all. You know that's our position; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Prosecution during this case, and we asked for a delay, and I've got to tell you I'm very grateful to a dear friend of mine who is a colleague in this courtroom, she is one of -- and she helped us find the document in the Croatian collection of intercepts that were in the EDS disclosure of approximately 10.000 or so pages given late in the trial several months ago; and there is a document that I want to show you here that I don't think we've seen since our case was over at that point. So can we have 2D642, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Finish your question. Have you finished it?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We're going to get it once the document is up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. In the meantime, Mr. Pandurevic, the previous question was: "Now do you know, sir, that our position is that Ljubisa Beara never had any intention to put or wasn't involved in any discussion to place POWs in Zvornik at all? You know that's our position; right?" What was your answer, I'm asking you to repeat it because it didn't show up in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said I knew that that was Mr. Ostojic's position. I don't know if it's anything other than a position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't know that he answered it that way before, but we're not going to debate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's look at this next exhibit to see if it's just my position or if the Prosecutor gave us finally some evidence that they themselves identify as exculpatory only after we brought it to their attention. So, Mr. Pandurevic, we've got this 10.000 plus intercepts from the Croatians that were taken. They were receiving intercepts from Belgrade, for example, other areas including the areas near or around Srebrenica, Vlasenica, Crna Rijeka, Zvornik, et cetera; but this intercept, in particular, we didn't get to review with any of the Prosecution witnesses because we didn't have it until late in the case. 2D642, it's in B/C/S. It's dated the 13th of July, 1995. Specifically I want to direct your attention to the time which is at 11.25 which is well or a couple hours after the intercept we have just seen where people were discussing putting something in Zvornik which was at 9.10, I believe. This intercept, if you see, doesn't capture a verbatim conversation, so we don't know exactly the source, but the Prosecution can help us with that. But look at what it says here, if you look at the last sentence there and you can read it out because we don't have it translated. It talks about people in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you let him read the full sentence?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Pardon me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Because we don't have a translation if he could read it all through, that would be helpful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm just excited about this intercept so I apologise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Could you read the entire intercept, Mr. Pandurevic, I'm sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes: "13th of July, 1995. 1125 hours, 924," that's probably some number: "Colonel Ljubo Beara (the Main Staff of the VRS) sending four buses, two lorries, and one trailer to Kasaba for the transport of captured Muslims. They will be taken to the camp in the Batkovici village where there will be a selection into various criminals and ordinary – into war criminals and ordinary soldiers."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now the word "selekcija" is in quotation marks, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, do you understand that to mean like there would be a triage or something, is that a synonym for that word, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military term is selection, it means making a distinction on some sort of basis between the wounded, those who are infected, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question was that -- the question really is: Why would the "selekcija" be in inverted commas because at the end of the day this is a transcript. Why would it be in inverted commas or quotes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know why the person who drafted this put it in inverted commas, perhaps he had some real doubts about the real purposes involved, the real objections involved. Perhaps he had something else in mind when the term selection was used, selection means some sort of sorting in my mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I put it to you, Mr. Pandurevic, that it is inverted commas because irrespective of whether the person who transcribed this thought the way you have explained it or not, he wanted to make sure that the exact word used was reported and that's why he or she put it in inverted commas, would you agree to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree with that if that's the only word that was literally transcribed as it was said, that's perhaps why it's in inverted commas.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, is it fair to say that as of the 13th of July, 1995 at 11.25 a.m., the intent, if you will, was to place Bosnian Muslims in the camp at Batkovci, was it not?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this conversation confirms what I have said. And with regard to what Obrenovic told me when speaking to Nikolic, it was said that people would be brought there, taken there, they'd be kept there for this triage and then sent to Batkovic [as interpreted] so on the 13th, that was the objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next exhibit, P1149, which is again the 13th of July and it's again the same one we looked at the Deronjic-Karadzic-intermediary discussion. Now these two civilians were talking on this intercept about moving goods, 2.000 or so, if you will, moving goods inside the warehouse or placing them somewhere else. So this is approximately eight or so hours later that same day from the prior intercept. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, do you agree with me that this conversation that same day on the -- there was a change from where they wanted to take the civilians made a decision as to where they were going to put those POWs, do you see that at all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is not being broadcast because it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in this conversation, they say that they should be placed in the warehouse or somewhere nearby, somewhere else. I don't know what they had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you reject the proposition that it was Deronjic who sent the POWs from Bratunac to Zvornik? Do you just reject that as a possibility given that -- and two days earlier, he was told to secure and he was named the commissioner in charge of the POWs or ...

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know who took the decision, according to which those prisoners from Bratunac should be transferred to the territory of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But do you reject the possibility or probability, based on this intercept, based on the exhibit that we saw, P10, Karadzic appointing Deronjic, then this discussion, P1149 on the 13th of July where they are discussing 2.000 of them or more and saying that they should be placed in warehouses and they should be placed somewhere else? As you sit here, don't you agree with me that it's possible, if not probable that it was Deronjic who moved the men from Bratunac where he was from to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can assume that he in some way participated in this event, but to what extent his decision was independent, was taken together with someone else, I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's look at P1206, please. Sir, this is an intercept, as it's coming up, that involves General Krstic, Captain Trbic, and through a switchboard operator, yourself, I think; but we'll let you talk about that, but I think you mentioned that in your direct. Now, I think the date of this intercept, just that we're clear is the 17th of July, 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm pretty sure it's the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We can agree it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I didn't want to scroll up and down, but thank you for that. Now, here, first, there is a discussion with General Krstic and Trbic. Again we shouldn't probably broadcast it and thank you for that. I want to focus just our attention here a little bit to know where everyone is because there is a switchboard operator that connected you through it. Trbic is where, at the command in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trbic was at the command in the office of the duty operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you, sir, you are in the IKM; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So you didn't -- and where was Krstic at the time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was in Vlasenica, whether the IKM or the call was there, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So the switchboard was able to connect you with Krstic first, with Trbic, and then ultimately with you at the IKM; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now let's look at the conversation first between Krstic and Trbic. And I know the preliminary stuff that makes identification of the people who are speaking and just below it says here Krstic says: "Okay have you killed the Turks up there?" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, Trbic responds by saying: "Well, I guess you got the report. What more can I tell you?" You see that obviously; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What report do you think Trbic is talking about?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably the report from the 16th that I sent interim combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And then Krstic says: "I got it." And Trbic responds by saying: "Basically we did?" Krstic says: "What?" Trbic says: "I said, basically we did." What is he referring to when he says, "basically we did," on two separate occasions, that he's killed the Turks?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the whole, yes, we did. He said, Has that been broken up? That's what Krstic asked. This conversation has to do with the events in Baljkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But I know you want to go to that next line where they then start talking about have they been broken up, but what is Krstic talking about right before that when he says: "Have you killed the Turks up there?"

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we have on the whole. He repeats the answer to the question put by Krstic, Did you kill the Turks up there, that had to do with the fighting in Baljkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now let's go down to where you're -- get brought into the conversation with Krstic. It starts by saying essentially: "Hello. Go ahead. This is Krstic. Hello, General, sir. Hello. Vinko. Vinko. Go ahead." And then what I want to look at here, Krstic says to you: "Are there any changes in reference to that report." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I know there was some discussion about you saying you wanted to, in your reports, to talk to Krstic. Here he's asking you about what report?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well it's the report dated the 16th, an interim combat report, at least that's what I had in mind, probably Krstic too.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, your response is he wanted to know if there's any changes to the report, you said: "Nothing significant." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Wouldn't that have been a good opportunity, if he's asking you about the report, to tell him what you've heard from Obrenovic or any others like Branjo Grujic about what you've heard with respect to any POWs that may have arrived in Zvornik that were not in your zone of defence?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that report, the 16th of July, nothing was said about that. It was in a report dated the 15th, and that's why Krstic didn't ask me about it, and I didn't mention anything about it to him; and this is something I have explained in the course of the examination-in-chief already.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All right. I didn't fully understand it, but here, Krstic is asking you, Are there any changes to your report? You're saying it's not the report of the 15th where you talk about the prisoners being distributed throughout the schools, you're saying it's the report of the 16th, and you're telling him there are no changes. Wouldn't that have been a good opportunity to say, Oh, but yes, General Krstic, I do want to tell you about these POWs that were brought here that I'm not responsible for and the activities that these people are claiming are occurring in the schools such as executions or burials.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could have had such thoughts, too, but I selected to act as I did, and you know how I gathered all the information, and how I relayed all that information in the interim combat report dated the 18th; and I also relayed that information when I subsequently had direct contact with General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever talk to Trbic about this intercept and what his -- what he meant when he said, "basically we did" in response to the question of Krstic: "Have you killed the Turks up there?"

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well how would I speak to him about this since I didn't know what they had previously been discussing? The first time I saw this intercept was here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right. I didn't -- I wasn't sure if you saw it before because I know you read Butler's report, and I know you met with Obrenovic, and I know you tried to get in contact with Semso Muminovic; so I wasn't sure if during that time when you were kind of -- before you were even indicted did you look at this intercept or is the first time you saw it was here when you came to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you can see with regard to intercepts in Butler's report, well, I saw all those things in the report, but as for all the other intercepts, the first time I saw him was here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at P1212 and it's A in English, Alpha, and D, Delta, in B/C/S. Sir, this is an intercept that purportedly is dated the 17th of July at 9.50 in the morning, and it's the first portion of the intercept that I'd like to direct your attention to. You're welcome to look at the entire intercept, but it's the last paragraph with the last X before the next intercept appears. Sir, just to further direct your attention, there are other references to you in that intercept. You're welcome to look at the whole thing but again I'm only going to focus for now your attention on the second -- or that last X in that intercept.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Have you seen this intercept before?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did here in The Hague along with the other intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, this one of the 17th of July at 9.50 they seem to be referencing you. I'm not suggesting, and it's not my burden of proof against you, or anything; but it mentions your name, so I just want to clarify. Do you remember this going on at all or this conversation? Where you say there were hundreds dead and someone is saying: "You can't kill them all there are so many of them. It's simply a living mass. You can't, let's say ..." and then it goes on to talk a is self-propelling gun, et cetera. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a conversation between two unidentified individuals who probably wanted to take a certain route, but they were not sure if it was safe. This was one of the examples how you spread rumours. They heard from certain sources about certain events and now they are evolving the situation, creating the situation, and interpreting it. The situation was, indeed, serious but not nearly as serious as they are portraying it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about did 20 of your men get killed that day, which is the paragraph right before that? That's pretty serious.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've seen in the report that there are dozens of killed, which means that we didn't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, the previous question from Mr. Ostojic which was in a way a compound question also asked you whether you remember this conversation. You don't seem to have answered that, at least that's how I read your answer to the previous question. Do you remember this conversation or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I said that I've seen this intercept along with other intercepts here in The Hague. I don't know who the people participating in the conversation are. I certainly am not one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I wanted that to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, and I understood it that way, Mr. Pandurevic. Thank you, Mr. President. Now let's look at P1310A, Alpha and D, Delta, in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This intercept, Mr. Pandurevic, is dated the 23rd of July, 1995, and I think it mentions Vinko, you addressed it, but it also mentions the first name of Ljubo. Can you just read that whole thing and let me know when you've had a chance to look at it or when you've completed your review.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The participant, it's, I think, the letter J, in inverted commas, from the previous conversation called again and asked for Vinko, but Ljubo answered. The question mark, in inverted commas, told Ljubo to "Pass on to Vinko, what Vinko and I were just talking about. Will" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, we have lost the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Talking about will arrive at your place by 1700 hours."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Pandurevic, they lost --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it the problem is solved. Because for a moment, the interpreters had lost the English translation, but we have it back now. So let's proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who is the Ljubo they are talking about in this intercept; do you know?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is probably Ljubo Bojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's be fair there is no doubt, is there, that it, in fact, is Ljubo Bojanovic they are talking about there; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we establish a connection with the previous conversation, then it is Ljubo Bojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then now let's go back to the duty officer notebook which is P377, please. And you have that, sir, in front of you. And I'd like to direct your attention to the last four numbers are 5759 of the ERN, so ERN last four numbers, 5759. I forgot to ask you this one question on that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At 1340 hours, it says: "Obrenovic to call Vuk urgently." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And we have some documents we'll show you in the tactical intercept that say that Vuk is actually Semso Muminovic, but you're saying Vuk is Dusko Vukotic, am I understanding you correctly, or did I miss that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was his code-name.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, and we'll see this a little bit later today when we looked at some of the evidence from another case and Mr. Muminovic's interviews with the Prosecution, he said your nickname was "Glovni" I think, do you remember that you had a code-name called Glovni?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You think that's what Muminovic said? Yes, I've seen it somewhere that he said that, but the code-name was not Glovni because, in that case, it wouldn't be a code-name.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll address it a little later when we get to that tactical intercept section, but here at 1340 hours, Obrenovic to call Vuk urgently. Is it your understanding that Obrenovic was to call Dusko Vukotic urgently?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what it's supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This is again just so we are clear on the 15th of July, 1995, and then down below at 1525 hours, it says duty officer from Zlatar is looking for the commander so he can brief him on the situation. Twenty-five minutes later, commander ordered tank company to go via Snagovo, et cetera. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me understand why Obrenovic needed to call Dusko Vukotic or Vuk urgently? I mean you were there, I think, approximately, at that time.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was at the IKM at the time. I think that Vukotic was at Kula Grad at the time. If he had some information from Obrenovic, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's turn to this exhibit, same one P377, ERN 5741. Sir, just let me know when you've had a chance to get to that page, please.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: These are kind of just clean-up questions for me. It says here, it mentions the name Ljubo on, I think, two occasions. And in the middle of the page right under the name of Mitar Zeljko, do you see that it's a reference to Ljubo to draw up our order, and again just so that everybody is following and the record is clear, I'm sorry, sir, this is an entry of the 13th of July, 1995. So I'm just asking for your assistance if you can tell us who you think this Ljubo is that they're referencing here on the 13th of July, 1995? Then it goes on to say, "To consult Dule or Petkovic." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably Ljubo Bojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, also below that, almost immediately, there is a reference again to Ljubo and it talks about two Pragas, self-propelled guns. Who are they referencing there; do you know?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably Ljubo Bojanovic again. As far as I know he was the only one by that name in the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The next page if you can turn to that I think starts with Vukotic and Petkovic, and the Prosecution was kind enough when they translated this to show us who signed which entry; and I note before the page before that I should have told you was apparently Sreten Milosevic according to them. The first section was also Sreten Milosevic's handwriting, but the section below that, they couldn't tell us whose handwriting that is because they don't know, and what I want to know is here it says Ljubo Dejanovic, do you see in the middle of the page. And we talked about that earlier today about all these different Ljubos in the Zvornik Brigade. And you didn't remember this guy, but if you look at it and maybe if we could -- yeah, it's there.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was corrected by someone. This should read Bojanovic. I am not familiar with this surname as it's written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's where I got it from. I looked it up and then I saw that. But now I asked you about the blue book that you have there, which we call the war diary, which is P378 about who had custody of it. Now, with respect to 377, do you know who maintained custody of Exhibit P377, the duty operations -- let me get the name right -- the duty officer notebook after December of 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know you've heard some evidence and discussion about it. Did it surprise you that Dragan Obrenovic had possession of this book at one time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I learned here during the trial, that it was in his possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And did you find out, not just from this trial but from any other source at any time whether Dragan Obrenovic made any changes or directed others like, let's say, Dragan Jokic to make changes or entries in this book?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We are now in open session, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President for helping me clarify that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to show you and discuss with you some of the witness statements that Mr. Muminovic gave to the OTP relating to the events of Srebrenica 1995, but just quickly for background, he was the individual with whom you negotiated the passage of the column on the 16th or thereabouts July, 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both the 15th and the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And he was what we call an enemy combatant; correct? He was on the other side of the war on the Bosnian Muslim side; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, let's look at his first interview, I think, that he has and that was the 8th of June, 2001, so it was before your attempt to call him because I know you talked to him or I think you mentioned you talked to him on the 5th of September, 2001. So this first interview I have a couple questions and it's P -- I'm sorry it's 2D635. Again, as always, Mr. Pandurevic, to you're welcome to look at the entire statement if you like I can provide it to you at the break or your counsel can, but I really want to look at the third page both in English and B/C/S and it says here ...

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you have a hard copy for me, perhaps, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can a hard copy be provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam usher, please. Thank you, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If she could show it to Mr. Haynes and the Prosecutor because there is some highlighting on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Pandurevic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I see Mr. Haynes consulting with his staff. Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: He's handed me the hard copy in a language I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I thought Mr. Pandurevic wanted it in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I understand, yeah, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just need it back to see what I highlighted it's that in English that I'm going to ask him about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey doesn't need to see it, so let's proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I could let you take some time looking at the whole document but Mr. Muminovic disagrees the reason why the column was opened. You gave your reason and you mentioned as a humanitarian you doesn't want to see people dying there. Mr. Muminovic says quite the opposite. He says he broke through the defence line, we're going to get into specifically what he says, I'm just giving you that background. You know that he takes a completely different position than you do as to the purpose and the rationale as to why the column was opened on the 16th of July, 1995. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted), and you testified about other people not being forthright and truthful. Do you think knowing what Mr. Muminovic said, do you think he's not being candid when he said that the reason the column was actually open was because the BiH broke through the Zvornik defence lines and we had actually encircled them; and there was a panic on their side and Mr. Pandurevic was begging me, because actually he uses the word begging, begging me to stop so we could open the column and get these guys out of here because they would have actually not only destroyed your whole brigade but probably the entire town? You know that's what he says, right, in a nutshell?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's not what he says. Some of that is true, but I think you should try to be a little more accurate than paraphrasing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It was just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And while we are at it because your questions are becoming longer and longer but in the meantime, there is another problem. Can we go to private session for a little bit? I need to point out something to you, Mr. Ostojic, Mr. Haynes, and Mr. McCloskey, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, we will get to the specific statement, and I think it's the third one that Mr. Muminovic discusses the reason for the opening of the corridor on the 16th of July in a little bit, and I got ahead of myself a little bit. I really want to focus with respect to this first statement, page 3, where Muminovic believed -- tell me when you've found it. It's in the middle of the page, it says: "Muminovic believed Pandurevic was in the Orahovac area near Lazete." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I note that at that time he is talking about in July -- you can see the reference immediately above that July 16th, 1995, and he talks about Obrenovic and his vehicle being seized during the operation, et cetera. Were you ever in Orahovac in the area near Lazete?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, at that time, I was commanding solely from the IKM. That is -- what you're referring to is a hole, and I couldn't see anything from a hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm only referring to what Mr. Muminovic is saying and I wanted to clarify that. On the next page of this document, page 4, Mr. Muminovic is talking about the negotiations between Obrenovic, Pandurevic, yourself, sir, and Muminovic on the 16th of July and then he talks about code-names being used; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This is where you've read also, and where I've gotten where we thought at least your code-name was Glavni, but you're telling us under oath that that's not correct; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are his assumptions and deductions. He didn't talk to Obrenovic at all, but he says here that he had radio contact with Obrenovic 20 times. On the first page, he says that on the 5th of May, he knew that an attack on Srebrenica was imminent. I didn't know that at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go then to the next exhibit, 2D636 which is an interview with the Prosecutor and Mr. Muminovic dated September 29th and October 1st, 2001. I'm going to try and see if I have a B/C/S version for you as well. With the Court's permission if we could ask the usher to show this to Mr. Haynes and the Prosecutor and then to the witness. As the Court can see while we're getting this to Mr. Pandurevic, there is certain sections redacted, and I think the Prosecutor is best able if the Court is interested to explain why; but that's the version we've always had in our possession, and that's just the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have no idea. I can figure it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't know that it's necessary but just so the Court and the record doesn't seem to indicate that we've redacted it. It was given to us that way and that's where it's at.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So if we can have, Mr. Pandurevic, you, take a look at this exhibit, 2D636; and as you can see there are certain pages that are completely blackened out or redacted or some reason, and the Prosecutor will let us know what that is all about and the only question I have was on the last page a couple entries with respect to this interview. Now, just so we have this time line down, this was taken again as I said September 29th and October 1st, 2001, which was approximately three or so weeks after you had this phone contact with Mr. Muminovic through Mr. Mijatovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably yes. I don't remember the exact date. If I spoke to him in September, and this is the end of September, then that's it. But I think that I've seen this statement unredacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You may have, sir, and we'll get to that at the next break but for my purposes I really wanted to focus on these two. If you prefer not to discuss that until you get the full version, I'll respect that and move to the next exhibit. Turn to the last page, if you will, and it talks about Muminovic's discussion with you at approximately 2000 hours on the 15th of July, and in the English version it says 15 July, 2001, but I'll let the Prosecutor tell us, I think that might be a mistake, it should be 1995, I think?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we looking at the same document? Could you compare the B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We are, but we're looking at the wrong page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you look at them they don't seem to be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's actually the last page in B/C/S is correct. We have that. We don't have the English version, page 4 which is the next page. Then now it should be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now it's okay. No, that's also on B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: English has only three pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm looking at the exhibit physically, and I have four pages so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's sort it out. If anyone has a hard copy of the fourth page in English which is -- seems to be missing from e-court, we can put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I thought we saw it just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, it was in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Perhaps we could use the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What you saw, what you saw on the left-hand side of the monitor, which to me also initially seemed to be the English translation was, in actual fact, the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about if we, with your permission, put this on the ELMO. There are two or three highlights, but I don't know that they really matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, I'm perfectly happy with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That part, I don't know. I don't know. I need someone to make sure that the last page, page four, which we don't have in e-court, has not been subject of a redaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You know what, Mr. President, he's going to find that out if we get the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can have the break now, but I need someone to check.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Page 4 is okay, I'm told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Not redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then you can put your question. Then you can put your question, and we'll have the break soon after.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record this document is the same as 3D546.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So would it be okay if I then retrieved the document and not put it on the ELMO, and then we can look at it through e-court? Thank you. I just want to make sure -- sorry. Thank you. Wow.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, and I'm sorry for that confusion on the document. Sir, I want to focus your attention as we see on the third or the fourth page of the English version where it says: "Muminovic believes he spoke to Pandurevic at approximately 2000 hours on 15 July." And as I stated earlier in English it seems to be 2001, but I think that's a mistake but we'll let the Prosecutor address that. I think it should be 1995. And that he believes, meaning Muminovic believes that, "Both Pandurevic and Obrenovic may have been aware of his, Muminovic's, knowledge of the murders outside the column." Do you know where Mr. Muminovic gets this information from?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did speak to me on the 15th, he didn't speak to Obrenovic though. He didn't mention any men being killed, and he couldn't have known whether anyone else had any information about this. I didn't know anything about it, and I didn't mention anything about it, and he didn't mention any killings to me either.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of July a day later, he also, while discussing this with the Prosecution, which is just a paragraph right below that, it's actually the last paragraph in this exhibit, he continues to say that he openly told you that he knew of the murders being committed and he goes on to say as we can see: " ... and that he begged Pandurevic to open a passage for the column and to stop killing the people in the column." Is that accurate or inaccurate from Mr. Muminovic's point of view?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can compare this with his previous statement when he said that he broke through the frontlines and made it possible for the columns to pass through. Here it says that he asked me to open up a corridor and to stop killing people in the column. What I said in the course of the examination-in-chief is the correct version.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just want to know because Mr. Muminovic was on your witness list. Did you talk to him about these issues when you guys put him on your list as a potential witness for your defence case? Did you say, Mr. Muminovic, you take a contrary position or -- strike that. You take a position saying, I knew about the murders. I didn't know on the 15th about the murders. I didn't know about on the 16th when we spoke. Did you have that kind of a discussion with him at all, with your witness?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't speak to him as if he were a potential witness. I spoke to him over the phone on two occasions. I didn't know he had given statements, and I didn't know what he had said in those statements. I never spoke to him about the events in Baljkovica on the 15th and 16th. He is on the list of witnesses, the 92 bis witness list but this has to do with a different period and different events. My Defence team never spoke to him about these events in Baljkovica, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now just because -- I don't know exactly when the break is, but I'm sure we'll find out. When you said at one point he said you were begging to open the column and this section it says he was begging. Really to concretely look at it we have to look at his third interview with the Prosecutor where they finally decided to get the facts in the case and that was from October 10th, 11th and 13th of 2001, but what I -- just in summary and we'll go through it specifically but in summary it says he wanted you to let the column go. You initially said no. They then advanced and made an action against the Zvornik Brigade, opened the defence line, encircled it, was about to crush it, then the table was turned, then he actually says that you were begging him to open the column up, so I don't know that they are mutually exclusive. He's saying initially he did beg for the column but later he took action and then he turned the tables on you and the Zvornik Brigade and then you were begging for it. Do you know that's what his position is in essence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's a fantastically compound question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic specialises in that. Shall we have the break, and you think how to break it down into a number of smaller questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Maybe I'll try. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Just to answer the question about that information report with the redactions on it. I've looked at that and that contained internal investigative information non-relevant to the information that was on the latter half of the report. Somehow that mixed up an information report with an internal information so that's why we had to do that but it should stay internal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, right before the break, I asked a long question as a foundation, and I'd like us to look at Exhibit 2D637, please. I'll try to break up my questions a little bit for you. As it's coming up, Mr. Pandurevic, I do have the B/C/S version if you prefer to have a hard copy, with the Court's permission and the usher's assistance, we can tender that to you of 2D637. Thank you very much. This is an interview with Mr. Muminovic on the 10th, 11th, and 13th of October, 2001, as indicated in the first page. Have you seen this interview and reviewed it prior to your testimony here these past few weeks?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read through this a long time ago, perhaps last year.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This is a lengthy interview of approximately ten pages although it has on the 11th and 12th page, witness acknowledgment and interpreter's certification. And I'd like to just direct your attention, if I may, to the sixth page in English, as well as in B/C/S, and it should be the entry that starts on the paragraph, "On 15 July, 1995."

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I want to give you an opportunity to review that, so if you could just take a moment and review that paragraph because I'd like to ask a question about it, and we'll read along also but to ourselves.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That first paragraph, Mr. Muminovic just says that he had a conversation with Obrenovic and that he requested him to let the people pass, not to kill anybody. And he has the date as the 15th of July, 1995. Did Obrenovic ever share that conversation with you when you met him at the command on the 15th of July, after 12.00 or 1.00 and forgive me for not knowing the precise time, but I thought it was always approximate after 12.00 when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to all the statements made by Obrenovic and on the basis of my own information and on the basis of conversations with Vukotic, Obrenovic did not speak to Semso on any occasion. Vukotic didn't, so did I.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Anyone else other than Dusko Vukotic and yourself that had conversations with Mr. Muminovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said that's the information I had. I certainly spoke to him on the 15th and on the 16th, Vukotic spoke to him on the 15th. As for Obrenovic, there is no information according to which he spoke to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so I get an answer to my question, so I'm correct that Obrenovic didn't share anything with respect to this portion that Mr. Muminovic claims that he spoke to Obrenovic, talked about letting the column go, and talked about not killing the people. Obrenovic never told you any of that; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn on the next page which is page 7 of both the English and B/C/S, and it's really the large paragraph basically in the centre of the page that I'd like to focus your attention on. And this is where Mr. Muminovic kind of explains his position with respect to why the column or the corridor was opened, so I know it's a lengthy paragraph but please take your time and read through it, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read through this lengthy passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm about to put a compound question. I'm going to break it down on a couple of issues that I'd like to discuss with you. In the fourth line at least in the English versions, on page 7 it says, it starts actually on the third line: "Since Jankovic had been arrested, Pandurevic was begging me to release Jankovic." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you were begging him to release Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We negotiated about this. It wasn't a matter of begging.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now the next few lines he's discussing Mr. Muminovic is, that he discussed with you opening the corridor letting the people go through, and then he states that: "Regardless of the negotiations, they continued with the ambushes in the area of Baljkovica." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do. No ambushes had been set up there, but the division had been blocked and surrounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then below that, the very next line, Mr. Muminovic is talking about the negotiations lasting until 2100 hours and then he talks about his military actions that he took that early morning about approximately 6.00 on the 16th where he attacked the Serbian front line, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did take action in the morning, offensive action, but he didn't succeed in doing what he says he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So far all he says is, I attacked the Serbian front line. Is that accurate, to the best of your recollection? It should be attacked the Serbian front line or the Serb front line, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He launched an attack, that's what I've just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From your answer, and then the next point I think you tell me if you disagree or agree with what Mr. Muminovic is saying, at that point, he says: "I broke the front line in Baljkovica. I seized the Obrenovic's forward command post and the battalion command and destroyed the firing position of the mortar 82 and 120 mm and captured Dragan Tesic." That's kind of the full sentence. Do you agree or disagree with what Mr. Muminovic is saying there?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. I don't know when Dragan Tesic was captured but they didn't break through the front line after the corridor had been opened up, some of their forces were sent through the corridor from the direction of Nezuk to help to get the wounded out and to help those who were leaving the 28th Division column. And on that occasion, they set fire to Praga and took that vehicle away.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then he goes on, and he continues, and we read it to ourselves, then he continues to say that he told you, apparently, at 1405 after you reached the final agreement to let the people from Srebrenica go and stop killing all civilians. Did you have that kind of a conversation with Mr. Muminovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to expand on this because otherwise I might go down the wrong route with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, be all means, Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much. The previous two statements that we saw, well one is from June, the other one from September. In the June statement, for the 16th, Mr. Muminovic says that he asked me to open a corridor. In the statement from September, it says that at 6.30 he broke through the front line. In this statement from October, we have a new version yet again but he insists on having established contact with me through Dragan Obrenovic; that's not correct. On the 16th in the morning, events continued to unfold, that is when wounded operations officer from the 28th Division were surrendered to Obrenovic. Obrenovic received information on the situation on the 28th Division, and that information was relayed to me and in the meantime, I had received other information that Semso was looking for me on the 16th and at about 10.00, I contacted him. I then offered him a cease-fire and the possibility of letting the column pass through. You have seen the intercepts when I say -- when I tell Obrenovic that I had reached an agreement with Semso. We would move our soldiers from the three trenches. We showed them the places that that would occur in, and we'd let the column pass through. I wouldn't conceal anything from Obrenovic. I wouldn't conceal the fact that the three trenches had been taken or that we would open up this area. If the 28th Division and the 2nd Corps had crushed me, everybody would have known about that. I would have conveyed all of that information to the corps, and I would have told them there was nothing I could do, and that I had been defeated in military terms. That would have been quite possible but that's not what happened. That's why my report from the 16th, my interim report, my interim combat report is such as it is and that is the whole truth, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to -- if you disagree with it and I don't know Mr. Muminovic at all, I just wanted to see -- really I just wanted to put it to you because it's there and I'm sure the Prosecution is going to ask this. So I'm not debating anything with you, sir. What I want to know is at the bottom of that page, page 7 on the English, and I think as well on the B/C/S version, Mr. Muminovic says that there was an intercept that was apparently captured. He calls it first an information report and if you read on which is the paragraph --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, directing your attention to the very next paragraph and again on this exhibit, on page 7 in English and B/C/S, Mr. Muminovic is talking about receiving an information report on the 16th of July. Two lines below that, he refers to it as an intercept and a conversation that he claims that you had with General Zivanovic, so I just want to direct your attention to that and let me know when you've read that full paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it and I've read through it, but I didn't speak to General Zivanovic. I don't know whether the document mentioned in the attachment -- mentioned as an attachment exists. Perhaps we can have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's what I was going to ask you. Did you have a conversation with General Zivanovic on the 16th about the --

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: About anything, right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't speak to Mr. Zivanovic at all on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Maybe the Prosecutor will be kind enough to get the document for us because when we got this material, those documents were not attached either so I haven't seen it. I just wanted to see what your thoughts were on that. Now, I'd like to direct your attention if I may to page 10 of the document or this exhibit, 2D637. Sir, this is where, just to orientate you on the document, it is when Mr. Muminovic is discussing his meeting with Miladin Mijatovic in Tuzla and where this exchange apparently with respect to a phone call happened. So if you could take a look at those three or so paragraphs, I'd like to ask you a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yesterday I told you about these conversations between myself and Semso after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who sent Miladin Mijatovic to meet with Mr. Muminovic in August or beginning of September 2001?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked Mijatovic to establish contact with him and to give me his phone number.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to speak to him on the phone. I said something about this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's why I'm just following up with this, with the document. The next paragraph here it says that in the last sentence in that fourth from the bottom paragraph, it says: "Pandurevic indicate that he had given interviews to 'Panorama' and other newspapers ..." do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but I don't remember giving any interviews to such newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say you're stating that you are not guilty of any crimes and that a Muslim commander could provide information on that topic. Did you discuss that at all with Mr. Muminovic in September, approximately, 5th of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know the exact date but I suggested, since I knew that he was familiar with the way events actually unfolded in Baljkovica on the 15th and 16th, I said if he wanted to be sincere and provide information in the form of an interview to the media, well, then, he could do so, so that the truth might come out because no one discussed these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you discuss with any news outlets your position as Mr. Muminovic indicates with either Panorama or other news agencies?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't even remember which newspapers are involved, "Panorama," and as for the other conversation over a land line, the other conversation with Mr. Muminovic, he suggested that he send a newspaper from Bosnia so that I could give him an interview about these events, but I didn't take him up on that suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's look just quickly since we are on the topic of Mr. Muminovic, the tactical intercept and we'll bring that up for you, which is P2232, I believe. And just so the Court is aware, the entire tactical intercept book was not translated but only certain portions so we -- there is a thick B/C/S version and we have just a few pages or so of the English version for the dates that I think are relevant. I said a few, but there's actually 29 just so that it's clear on the record. I don't know if we have the original, and if we do, we just ask maybe it would be easier for Mr. Pandurevic to have the original when he reads or answers questions. You do not. Okay. I have a hard copy --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can get it, but, of course, we don't have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think we can still go through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to orientate you to a couple of points in this intercept or these tactical intercepts, and we talked a little bit about code-names but I'd like for you to find, if you can, on the 13th of July, and I'll give the ERN number --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Does the witness have the B/C/S version in front of him in any format all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you, Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't have the B/C/S version or the page that Mr. Ostojic is referring to in English either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I could help. It is P2231. It is B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The English version is P2232, the B/C/S version is P2231.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I can give him mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can move now, it should be up.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we can be directed to the B/C/S ERN 0084-8949, which is approximately eight pages from the start of the exhibit. Just so we can orientate ourselves, we're trying to find the entry at 2050 hours and on the English page it's page 3, the bottom of the page. At 2050, it proceeds to say: "Lovac 1 reported to Lovac."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, here, I just wanted again for you to tell us if you know who Lovac 1 was and who he was reporting to?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lovac 1 was Dragan Obrenovic, and Lovac was the radio communications centre according to the plan of communications network that he had designed and which he discussed in his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And just for the English speakers, we're going to turn to the next page, page 4, but for B/C/S, we're still staying on this 949 page and there's a discussion there about a vehicle, there's a discussion about "Premijer," and that's still on the 13th because I think if you look at the date right underneath it at least in English it shows that it's the 14th, but I'm presuming that, you correct me if I am wrong, and then it talks about in parentheses, it has the name Ljubo, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who are they talking about here?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About Ljubo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know, but do you know which Ljubo?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume that it's Ljubo Bojanovic, if this person is attached to the Zvornik Brigade. If he is not, I don't know who he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who are the other people that they are referencing there "Premijer" and ...

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We said that "Premijer" was the code-name for the radio intercept station of the Zvornik Brigade, the other names are code-names of the units that took part in the blockade of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if you turn the page, sir, they are talking and the same page in English, page 4 on the next day which is the 14th of July, and I'll have to concede this, Mr. Pandurevic, you may not be able to read the B/C/S version because I think the copies are actually rather poor, that's basically how we received them and I guess that's the way it is. At 1330, it has a conversation with Roki, and this would be on ERN 8950, it has at 1330 Roki and Omega requested a package from Roki. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it in English but not in the Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I think that will be okay. What are they referring to here, a package?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A certain Roki and Omega are talking but I don't know whose code-names these are, and what kind of packages they are referring to, whether they are referring to human beings or something else, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who was Roki and Omega?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He just told you that he doesn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I was flipping the pages, thank you, Mr. President, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's then go to the 15th of July, which is in the English pages 8 through 14 and for you, Mr. Pandurevic, we should start, I think, at the last three numbers being 953 on the B/C/S version. That's where it starts just so he can see the date but then I'll direct his attention when he cease the numbers the last three numbers 957 in the B/C/S, and page 13 in the English. So again, sir, just to orientate ourselves, it seems to be that this is a tactical intercept from the 15th of July, and I want to focus your attention on the entry that starts at 1345 and it says: "Vuk spoke to Zukov again ..." and you just let me know when you've seen that.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it in English, but I can't see it in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Are we okay to proceed, but I think in the B/C/S it would be 8957 are the last four ERN numbers. Then we're looking at the entry at 1345.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, immediately the third line underneath that it talks about Igman and Igman 1, and who are they again?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Igman was artillery, as far as I remember, the mixed artillery battalion, and Igman 1 was one of its units.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next paragraph or next few lines we tried to -- I covered it yesterday in part asking you who Vuk was, Ikar, Pavle; do you see that entry there, those three individuals?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do. I said yesterday that Vuk was Vukotic, that was his code-name for the most time and that probably that was the name used at that time as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It identifies the three people, Vuk, Ikar and Pavle, and I know that you said Dusko Vukotic negotiated with Mr. Muminovic as did you, but Obrenovic did not. The entry I want to get your -- get an answer to this, it says: "I talked to Semso (Vuk) and stopped the activities." Who, other than you, sir, was talking to Semso and who other than you -- well I don't want to make a compound question. We'll stop there. Who other than you and Dusko Vukotic were talking to Semso Muminovic on the 15th of July after 1345 hours?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if anyone else spoke to him. Maybe somebody from the MUP. All I know is that I and Vukotic spoke to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then it goes on to say: " ... stopped the activities." Who other than you, sir, was able to stop the activities?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see clearly here in the original whether a proposal was made to stop the activities or if they had actually been stopped. I would appreciate if this page can be enlarged, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We're going to try also, Mr. Pandurevic, to get the original so that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The original is in evidence as you may recall when the witness came. It is gettable, that will take a bit of time. We can try right now, but it seems like it may be worth waiting to get the original as opposed to this -- what's -- what sounds like guess work and I don't think the witness should rely on the English. And on another topic, the intercept that was the attachment of the Muminovic statement, I am told is 65 ter 1183 from 16 July, 0706 hours if you want to get it up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. In the meantime, is it possible to zoom in further? Maybe that will make it easier for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you work with that, Mr. Pandurevic, or do you want it ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to read, Your Honours. "Vuk, Ikar, Pavle, I spoke with Semso (Vuk) and stopped the activities. They are --" [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Pandurevic, they haven't translated it, so I don't mean to stop you. They stopped, actually, where you said they care for the head of the column, soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They stopped at -- the interpretation stopped with the words "and stopped the activities. Then you continued reading. If you could repeat it again slowly, Mr. Pandurevic. Let's zoom in a little bit further. I think we can still do that. Understanding that will make it easier. Can you start again from after the word "activities."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, certainly. " ... they care about the head of the column (army). I suggested to him that they let all those from the central prison in Tuzla and we shall -- these -- Pavle, we cannot --" I can't make out this word, and then it says "negotiations." I think it says something like we are not authorised to negotiate. What is Semso saying about the captured policemen, he says that they were there alive and so on and so forth. Shall I keep on reading, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. Mr. Ostojic, do you need him to read more?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I thought the Court asked him to read it but no, that's fine for this point right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I want to break it down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I know you don't know or you told us who the people are: Vuk, Ikar and Pavle. It says here that there was a suggestion to release all those from the central prison in Tuzla, and in English we have here "and we would release these," so who other than you were negotiating with Mr. Muminovic because it seems from this tactical intercept on the 15th of July at 1345 hours, whoever these three people are, they certainly knew that there was some prisoners and there was a discussion on exchanging some from Tuzla with those that they were keeping, meaning "they", the Zvornik Brigade, in essence?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, you understand this conversation perfectly well. Look at it once again. The persons talking are Vuk, Ikar, and Pavle, and the signalsman on the Muslim side who was recording this. Vuk speaks first and says, I spoke to Semso. It's the signalsman who put Vuk in parentheses which means that Vuk spoke to Semso, and the activities were stopped, "and they care," and that is what Vuk is saying, "they care about the head of the column," and it was Vuk who suggested that they release all those from the central prison in Tuzla and we shall release these. It is Vuk who is proposing the cease-fire and the cessation of combat, not Pavle or Ikar. Pavle said that he was not authorised to negotiate.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that, but my point is that Vuk was a member of the Zvornik Brigade. You told us that his name was Dusko Vukotic, he on the 15th of July, 1995, at 1345 hours, he's talking about exchanging prisoners that he has, isn't he, with those that Bosnian Muslims have from the central prison in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Vuk says "these men," he's referring to the 28th Division. Since you are pushing me to the limit, you persistently avoid a conversation where Ljubo did not take part, only his surname was mentioned. After Krstic had send me to Zvornik to fight the 28th Division, he asked 20 or 30 men from Krstic to deliver packages or distribute packages. Vukotic had no men to offer for exchange. If he was referring to the 28 columns the one who was asking for this to be sent was on my doorstep to put it figuratively, but he says you'd better speak to Vasic or Obrenovic don't speak to Pandurevic although it he is close to you because he wouldn't dare speak to me about this or he didn't trust me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, I'm sorry if you think that I'm pushing you to the limit, that's not my intent. I just wanted clarification on this intercept. If you don't mind, if we can proceed with the next passage which in English appears on page 14, and I think it continues on the same page in B/C/S although they would have to probably scroll -- I think it's actually good there because it's immediately before the 1510 entry and the word Pavle and Pekos, so we pretty much have it. Again, sir, this is a tactical intercept after 1345 but before 1510 hours on the 15th of July, 1995. We have the English translation, but I just want to make sure that you can read that, those four or five lines because you'd like to ask you a couple questions about that.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I read the last three lines out loud?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If the Court would like you to you can, but for my purposes you don't just the Court indicated earlier to read so ...

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Here, they are discussing a captured policeman and if anything happened to him, and then someone says it will be 100 for 1; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously someone from the police was inquiring about these policemen and this person Pavle could be someone from the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say Pavle told him not to negotiate with him so just so I'm right -- make you could tell us it's Pavle telling Vuk not to negotiate with Mr. Muminovic; correct? Did I get that right at least?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. Pavle was passing instructions to him not to negotiate.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If Pavle is with the MUP possibly, why would he be giving instructions to one of your men in the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in contact. They were talking to each other. Maybe this man thought that was a better approach. But if I had given this order, why would I be negotiating afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm only asking to clarify this, I'm not testing you on. It goes on to say: "We'll kill them in the and he can fire at Serbia, Belgrade, Zvornik as much as he wants" the next sentence I wanted to get your thoughts on and he says: "Tell him that all of them should surrender in Orahovac." Again, 15th of July after 1340 hours and apparently before 1510 hours, what was happening in Orahovac that they would be surrendering and who is surrendering? I mean why Orahovac of all places? Did Pavle and this guy, Vuk, know what was happening in Orahovac at that time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody surrendered in Orahovac at that time. Unfortunately on the afternoon of the 14th, all those who were held prisoner in Orahovac were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But my question is: Why would he tell him, who is the "him" that all of them should surrender in Orahovac? Is Pavle telling Dusko Vukotic or is Dusko Vukotic telling Pavle or what?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tell him to have them all surrendered in Orahovac. I don't know what this means and what he wanted to say. What I know is that at the time mentioned here, there was no one held prisoner in Orahovac. Even all those who were shot dead on the 14th had been buried by that time and that was a fact established in the course of this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, you don't know -- you didn't know that information on the 15th of July, 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, I said that a few times.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you didn't know that information on the 16th of July, 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the evening of the 16th, I knew that men had been shot dead in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When we look at this entry, do you think, to the best -- if you answer this -- do you think Pavle and Vuk or Ikar that they knew what was happening in Orahovac, and that's why they are asking for the rest of the column to surrender in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
