utterances.text: It's just an invitation to speculate. It's also about four questions at the same time. He is a factual witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, if we could look at the July 16th entry which is 8958 in B/C/S and page 15 in the English version. I only bring this up because you mentioned some intercept that you talked about on your direct examination but -- and it starts at 32 and I, or 1, talked, "A package went up there ten minutes ago." This again just so you know, I think it's the 16th of July, 1995, at 8.15. Just let me know when you've seen it.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what package they're talking about?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says 31 and 2 talked, maybe it was radio package communication, whether it was the form of the communication that took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Skipping along the next couple of pages which is page 19 in the English version and 8961 in the B/C/S. The entry is 1100 hours "Lovac 1 and Palma, the road is free."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction it should be radio packet communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, just to direct your attention this again, I believe, from looking at it is the 16th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see where it says that the road is passable or free. I suppose that it's where the cursor is but this word is not clear. I can only discern the road is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay and that's okay because that's not really -- my question was just directing your attention to that paragraph. I really want to -- if you can find where Palma asks Lovac 1: "Are the Turks at the school?"

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And this is on the 16th of July, 1995 at approximately 1100 hours. Do you have any information as to what Palma and Lovac 1, who is Obrenovic, were talking about when they were asking: "Are the Turks at the school?"

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would you share that with us?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was Palma, Lovac 1 was Obrenovic, and the reference was made of the old school in Baljkovica close to the defence line, and if you look at the map, you will see the letter SH [as interpreted], which stands for school.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll get that map. I was hoping to have it today, but we'll get it for sure on Monday, and we'll go through it a little bit. Now, we couldn't hear what Lovac 1 says and what did he say in response to this when you asked him: "Are the Turks at the school?"

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I honestly don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps yes, perhaps no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to clarify, is it SH for school or some other letters?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's SK, I think the witness says in B/C/S but I think they just translated it, it's SK I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's my question. We got SH so I just want to clarify that if it's going to be a map reference, especially.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We don't have the map here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But to the best of your recollection, Mr. Pandurevic, the reference to the school was abbreviated Sk; right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there's a topographic sign and it's marked S, capital S. That's the diacritic and small k.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now talking about this entry here, it talks about the men from Bratunac as well, a line or two above that and the men from Bratunac from time to time we've seen some reference that we were in Orahovac. Now, here it says, "Palma personally orders them to conquer elevations above the school." What I'd like to know from you is what school is that? I know in the second portion of that when I asked you are the Turks at the school, you told us that, but now there's another entry of school so I wanted to make sure it's maybe the same, but I'd rather have you answer it than me speculate.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same school in Baljkovica, the old school. And these are the men who came to the 4th Battalion --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, Mr. Pandurevic, please, for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. So this is the same school in Baljkovica, which was burned down at the time. The men from Bratunac are the unit from Bratunac that had arrived on the 15th and deployed in the defence zone of the 4th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I see that they've given you, I think, the tactical intercept original P2231; correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And with all due respect since we covered it, but perhaps not as -- since we didn't have the original, and we did have some trouble reading it, if I can direct your attention, again, to the entry, and that would be on the B/C/S last four numbers 8957 which was the entry on the 15th of July at or after 1345 hours. I think if you find that 1345 then we would be able to orientate ourselves to it and on the English it's page --

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And on English it's page 13 and then proceeding on page 14.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can even see some additional words.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Would you be kind enough, and I apologise for having to ask you this again, to read that section again where it starts with Vuk, Ikar, Pavle, so that we could get it and then we could all appreciate, perhaps, what it says. Out loud if it's okay with Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I start reading this out, when it says 1345 well could I start reading out from there? It says: "Vuk spoke to Zukov again and agreed on a truce." Then supposedly there were to be negotiations. Later he fired a shell, 1 for 1. Igman, Igman 1. Put to all fighting, 1410 hours. Then it goes on: "Vuk-Ikar-Pavle, I spoke to Semso (Vuk)," so he spoke to him, "and stopped the action. They care for the head of the column (soldiers). I suggested that he release all of those from the central prison in Tuzla and we would release these. Pavle -- we don't have a mandate for negotiations or authority to negotiate." So this word "mandate" is not a word that I previously saw it in the copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think they got it in English so thank you for that. Sir, with respect to this now having looked at the original, what Vuk and Pavle are talking about is an exchange of prisoners to exchange the prisoners that the BiH had for the prisoners that the Zvornik Brigade had. When they talk about: "I suggested him to release all those from the prison and we would release these." It doesn't say you'd open the column or create a corridor for the column to pass, he's specifically talking about POWs, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's your interpretation, but I absolutely disagree with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And basically it's because at that time, you were under the impression that you had no prisoners on the 15th of July at approximately or after 1345 hours; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's correct, I didn't know -- I didn't even have any prisoners, Mr. Ostojic, someone else had on the 13th, 14th and 15th. I didn't ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that you did personally, sir, and I'm just saying that maybe the Zvornik Brigade didn't tell you because it looks like they didn't give you a lot of information, and they didn't keep you well informed or abreast of everything that was happening, especially when you see the involvement of this Colonel Dragomir Vasic with the 6th Battalion from time to time. So I just want to clarify this point one more time. Maybe this person, Vuk, and maybe this guy, Pavle, knew, but you didn't; but they're talking pretty clearly here it seems to me about exchanging prisoners.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, they're talking about a column, about the column. They were talking about leaving the column. I didn't know who was in the central prison in Tuzla. Vasic was in a better position to know something about that as he was a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Now, you told us when you were -- in 1993, you also negotiated a passage of a column at that time, again I think you said without having the authority to do that from the higher or corps command or Main Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that. And you weren't -- were you at all reprimanded, disciplined as a result, in 1993, of opening this column?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I quite simply didn't want to fire on the column, and I didn't want to prevent it from passing through. I let it pass through.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, what I'm asking you did the corps or the Main Staff or any military organisation reprimand, discipline, or sanction you in any way for opening a column which wasn't authorised?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that time, they didn't even know anything about the circumstances under which all of this occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I know it's late, but I don't mean like right that day or that next day, I mean ultimately, a week, a month, a year later when they found out, or maybe they still don't know. But they -- at no time were you ever disciplined or reprimanded or sanctioned as a result of opening up a corridor in 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't officially sanctioned punished or reprimanded. It was war and they needed me while the fighting continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well I'll let you or someone else talk about this official or unofficial stuff. In fact, after that you were promoted from major to Lieutenant-Colonel, were you not? That was from 1993 you were a major, and then you were promoted to lieutenant-colonel on June 23rd, 1994?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Pandurevic, that they didn't reprimand sanction or discipline you in any way because they agreed with your decision; would that be right?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the decision was taken by myself, it had been carried out and after the event, there was nothing they could do to prevent that from happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In November of 1993, did the Zvornik Brigade negotiate a truce and a prisoners exchange? And again, sir, November 1993?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How many prisoners at that time did the Zvornik Brigade have?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I think there were two or three prisoners who were captured in the immediate vicinity of the front. I can't remember all the details now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, do you remember if the enemy side gave you a list of persons it was interested in for exchange?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure. I think we had two of their prisoners and they had one of our men, and we organised an exchange. That should be in the documents somewhere. They were prisoners who were captured at the front line itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there ever a temporary battalion set up for combat operations in Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A temporary battalion didn't exist in Rocevic. At the beginning of 1995, we trained men. We would take young soldiers to that area and train them there. There was never a temporary battalion there. There were soldiers from all battalions in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And that special -- or that scheduled training for combat operations, you conducted that in Rocevic as well as in Orahovac; correct?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember that in Rocevic, the features were such that it was possible for us to provide the training we wanted to provide, and I was there for a while and followed the training provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Orahovac, I'm not sure. When the line in Memici was taken, I know that a unit was established or set up and went to Memici to the line, but as for training in Orahovac, no, I can't remember anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll ask a couple more questions before we break. Whose zone or area of responsibility was that in Rocevic where the scheduled training for combat operations was being conducted?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We provided training. We weren't involved in combat operations there. It wasn't a training ground. It was a state-owned land.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me just show you quickly because we only have a few minutes 7D454, and I think you've seen this document, it's a report dated the 11th of November 1993 signed by Nenad Simic. And I think we looked at it to see that he was the assistant commander for moral guidance, religious and legal affairs, and I have the B/C/S hard copy if you'd like, but I don't know that it's necessary because I'm sure it's in e-court. Sir, I just want you to see the first page there, and then if you look under paragraph 3, in English it would be the second. Page, it talks about training of the temporary battalion. I didn't read your report, but it seems to have a temporary battalion there and then it talks and I'll let you catch up so you can answer the question. But it says in the first sentence and I'll read it: "The scheduled training for combat operations of the newly-formed temporary battalion is underway in Rocevic and Orahovac."

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that training was to take place in Orahovac too and I don't remember that training there. I remember Rocevic. Well, I know that there are no good features in Orahovac which would make it possible for the kind of training that we wanted to be provided, to be provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pandurevic. I have about, Mr. Pandurevic, so you know as well, approximately an hour and a half but no -- I don't believe any more. I'll try to shorten it when I look at this and to the extent that I can conclude in short order, I would on Monday, if acceptable. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course that is acceptable, Mr. Ostojic. We'll adjourn today, resuming Monday morning at 9.00. Thank you.
